correctness.rationale: Brown and Hoshino's Theorem 4.9, verified in the primary text, gives the exact four-round cutoff 11 for individual cycles. Cartesian-product adjacency is a Boolean combination of factor equalities and adjacencies, so coordinating the two winning factor strategies gives a four-round product win. Thus every pair reduces to the 45 unordered dimension pairs in [3,11]. The recursive atomic back-and-forth type is complete for first-order quantifier rank four, including all repeated choices and Boolean combinations. The embedded Python-standard-library program computes the exact types for all 45 pairs in two independently represented ways, proves agreement of their partitions with the explicit table, obtains exactly 19 classes, and identifies the final class with canonical pairs of dimensions at least eight. Truncation cannot increase order, so that class forces the sharp 64-vertex bound within the family. Six outside-cutoff trials are auxiliary consistency tests, not used as proof of the infinite assertion.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies every member of a natural infinite two-parameter, vertex-transitive, four-regular graph family by all bounded-rank-four FO sentences. It gives exactly 19 classes and the sharp minimum universal torus-grid representative order 64, neither a mere restatement of individual cycle equivalence nor a one-off small graph computation. A notable structural feature is stronger logical stabilization under Cartesian product: each cycle factor remains distinguishable at lengths 8 and 11, yet all products with both factors at least 8 are rank-four equivalent. The finite exact type data are reusable as a testing kernel; no unsupported algorithmic downstream theorem is claimed.
